classification.difficultyReason: Multiply probabilities for each independent guess pattern, use the all-wrong complement and count the three distinct positions of the wrong guess when exactly two are correct.

content.prompt: Bob guesses three questions in his multiple choice exam, which has four options per question. Find the probability that Bob gets

answer.worked:
Each independent guess has probability $\frac14$ of being correct.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{all correct})&=\left(\frac14\right)^3\\P(\text{all correct})&=\frac{1}{64}\end{align*}$$

The probability of a wrong guess is $\frac34$. Use the complement of all three guesses being wrong.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one correct})&=1-\left(\frac34\right)^3\\P(\text{at least one correct})&=1-\frac{27}{64}\\P(\text{at least one correct})&=\frac{37}{64}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{9}{64}$

The incorrect guess can be any one of the three guesses.
answer.worked:
There are three positions for the incorrect guess. Each pattern has two correct guesses and one incorrect guess. Let $A$ be the event of exactly two correct guesses.

$$\begin{align*}P(A)&=3\times\frac14\times\frac14\times\frac34\\P(A)&=3\times\frac{3}{64}\\P(A)&=\frac{9}{64}\end{align*}$$
